task.name: Nothing surfaces what a well-formed issue body requires, so an author discovers each rule by submitting a body and reading the refusal
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2725
---

## Why

An author cannot find out what a well-formed issue body requires except by writing one and
submitting it. The rules are real, mechanical and enforced — required sections, the distinction
between a description and an implementation plan, and a fixed vocabulary of verbs an acceptance
criterion must use to count as observable — but they live in the checker's own source and are
surfaced only as a refusal after a body already exists.

The cost is a rewrite loop per issue. In one session on 2026-08-12, filing two issues took five
refusals: an acceptance section with no verb from the accepted vocabulary, then an example read as an
implementation plan because it showed a call sequence, then the same finding again for naming file
paths, then the verb vocabulary a second time on a rewritten body, then again on a third issue. Every
one of those rules is stable and knowable. None of them was knowable to the author before submitting.

This is separate from making the pipeline mandatory, which is tracked elsewhere. Enforcement answers
"can an author go around the tooling"; this answers "does an author who wants to comply have any way
to know what compliance is before being refused." An authoring surface that asks for what it needs is
also the cheapest form of enforcement, because it makes the pipeline the path of least resistance
rather than the path that rejects you.

The refusal behaviour this issue builds on already exists and works: a draft too thin to classify is
kept as a draft and answered with structured questions rather than force-classified. That is the same
shape wanted here, moved earlier — asked while the body is being written rather than after it is
submitted.

## Example

Today, an author writes a full body, submits it, and is told one rule at a time:

```
submit  -> refused: no acceptance criterion contains an observable verb
submit  -> refused: body contains implementation-plan content
submit  -> refused: body contains implementation-plan content (file paths)
submit  -> accepted
```

Wanted, before anything is submitted:

```
what kind of work is this?                    enhancement
what does it emit, return, or write when done? ...
  (an acceptance criterion states an observable outcome; describing how to
   build it belongs in the plan phase, not here)
```

The author is told the constraint at the moment the constraint applies, and the first submission
passes rather than the fourth.

## Acceptance criteria

- An authoring path exists that collects a body's required parts before submission and reports what
  is still missing, so an author is never refused for a rule they had no way to read.
- Where a required part has a constrained form, the constraint is stated at the point that part is
  collected, expressed as the property the part must have rather than as an enumeration the author
  selects from. An acceptance criterion asks for an outcome a reviewer could check, and structural
  admission never depends on matching a fixed vocabulary — the authoring path does not make the
  author select from a word list, and no closed list is presented as the definition of
  observable. Whether a criterion is meaningful remains a semantic question, which review may
  still challenge.
- A body produced through the authoring path passes the shape gate without a rewrite loop, and where
  it cannot, the path reports which part is still short rather than emitting a body that will be
  refused.
- The authoring path parses and renders through the shared typed specification rather than
  carrying its own idea of the required parts, and validates the finished object through the
  same evaluation every other surface consumes before it submits anything.
- The authoring path accepts an existing draft as a starting point, so a captured todo can be
  completed rather than restarted.
- Where an author declines to supply a required part, the path writes a draft that is honestly marked
  incomplete rather than one that reads as ready.

## Out of scope

Preventing or detecting issues authored outside the pipeline, which is tracked separately. This issue
assumes an author who wants to comply and asks only whether compliance is discoverable.

handoff.summary: Added an interactive `forge author` flow that collects required typed-issue parts before submission, resumes local drafts or existing `todo:draft` issues, replaces incomplete modeled sections via the shared document API, validates through the shared shape gate before any GitHub mutation, and writes honestly marked incomplete drafts when required content is declined. The CLI was wired into `main.py`, docs were updated in the authoring guide and CLI reference, and regression tests cover both the pure intake flow and the CLI seam.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The new authoring path is present, but incomplete-session persistence and existing-issue promotion can lose or mislabel draft work. | [anthropic-opus-cli] forge author works for fresh enhancement/bug/task drafts, but resuming a saved draft leaves the stale incomplete-draft banner inside the finished body, and the epic/operator-action types it offers can never complete.

findings.description: When a bug author supplies some missing Diagnosis fields and then leaves a later Diagnosis field blank, the returned incomplete draft drops the fields already supplied and reports only the first declined field as missing.
When forge author --create reaches an incomplete body without --output, it refuses submission without writing or printing the incomplete draft.
When promoting an existing draft issue and the title/body edit fails after label changes succeed, the command can remove todo:draft from the old draft body and leave it looking promoted.

Resuming a saved incomplete draft leaves the generated banner line 'Status: incomplete draft — do not submit yet' inside the finished body, so a completed, gate-passing issue is written out and filed still carrying the do-not-submit notice, and a second incomplete pass stacks another copy of the banner on top of the first.

The --type flag offers 'epic' and 'operator-action', but a fully answered body of either type is always classified as a draft, is stamped with the incomplete-draft banner and todo:draft, and is refused at --create, so choosing either type leaves the author in a loop with no answer that can ever finish, and for operator-action the reported reason list is empty so the banner says only that shape-gate findings remain.

A draft file with no frontmatter title and no leading level-one heading yields the file stem as the issue title, and because that value is non-empty the flow never prompts for a title, so a resumed draft can be filed under a title such as 'draft' or 'notes'.

When the shape gate refuses for a reason outside the small mapped set — for example a bug whose confirmed cause is stated as unknown, which refuses as diagnosis_cause_unknown — the missing-parts list stays empty and the draft banner reads only 'Missing before submission: shape-gate findings remain'.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 names shape_check.document.with_section as the merge API for collected answers, but that function immediately returns the document unchanged when the section key already exists. Consequently, an existing draft containing an empty or placeholder ## Acceptance criteria, or a partial ## Diagnosis, cannot be completed: validation will report it as short, but the planned flow has no data path for applying the author's replacement or missing fields. Step 6 tests only collection of entirely missing sections, so this AC-relevant failure is not caught.
  Suggestion: Add an explicit document operation for replacing or merging the body of an existing modeled section, use it when gate findings identify an existing section as short, and test resuming both a placeholder acceptance-criteria section and a partial diagnosis section.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 says to 'register its parser in build_parser()' and re-export cmd_author from cli/__init__.py 'following the existing shape/groom/todo patterns'. main.py actually delegates to per-module register_parser(subparsers) (main.py:90-98) plus a dispatch dict (main.py:137-145), and cli/__init__.py re-exports cmd_todo but not cmd_shape/cmd_groom — so the cited pattern is not uniform.
  Suggestion: Follow the todo.py shape: add author.register_parser(subparsers) and 'author': author.cmd_author to the dispatch map; the __init__ re-export is optional and should match whichever neighbour the dev picks.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5 documents forge author only in docs/guides/authoring.md, but docs/guides/cli-reference.md carries a per-command section for every CLI verb (e.g. ## forge todo at cli-reference.md:854). A new top-level command absent from the reference leaves the discoverability surface this story exists to fix half-covered.
  Suggestion: Add a short ## forge author entry to docs/guides/cli-reference.md alongside the authoring.md section, cross-linking rather than duplicating the constraint prose.

finding_registry.description: When a bug author supplies some missing Diagnosis fields and then leaves a later Diagnosis field blank, the returned incomplete draft drops the fields already supplied and reports only the first declined field as missing.
When forge author --create reaches an incomplete body without --output, it refuses submission without writing or printing the incomplete draft.
When promoting an existing draft issue and the title/body edit fails after label changes succeed, the command can remove todo:draft from the old draft body and leave it looking promoted.

Resuming a saved incomplete draft leaves the generated banner line 'Status: incomplete draft — do not submit yet' inside the finished body, so a completed, gate-passing issue is written out and filed still carrying the do-not-submit notice, and a second incomplete pass stacks another copy of the banner on top of the first.

The --type flag offers 'epic' and 'operator-action', but a fully answered body of either type is always classified as a draft, is stamped with the incomplete-draft banner and todo:draft, and is refused at --create, so choosing either type leaves the author in a loop with no answer that can ever finish, and for operator-action the reported reason list is empty so the banner says only that shape-gate findings remain.

A draft file with no frontmatter title and no leading level-one heading yields the file stem as the issue title, and because that value is non-empty the flow never prompts for a title, so a resumed draft can be filed under a title such as 'draft' or 'notes'.

When the shape gate refuses for a reason outside the small mapped set — for example a bug whose confirmed cause is stated as unknown, which refuses as diagnosis_cause_unknown — the missing-parts list stays empty and the draft banner reads only 'Missing before submission: shape-gate findings remain'.

Resuming an issue whose only type label is epic selects the epic type through the inferred-label branch before the dispatchable-type filter is applied, so the flow runs a type that can never reach a runnable result, stamps the completed body with the incomplete-draft banner, proposes adding todo:draft, and refuses submission no matter what the author answers.

The catch-all branch that turns unmapped gate reasons into missing parts does not distinguish blocking findings from advisory ones, so a body refused for implementation-plan content is also told that a Missing Example part is required before submission even though the example section is advisory for that type and decides nothing.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

steps.description: Create the core authoring flow as reusable intake logic.
steps.details: Implement a stdlib-only flow that accepts a title, selected type label, optional existing body/labels, and injected answer source. Resolve the selected type through `spec_for_label`/`IssueTypeSpec`, parse any existing draft with `parse_issue_document`, inspect required/forbidden sections via `SectionRule` and `Presence`, add collected section bodies with `with_section`, render with `render_issue_document`, and validate the finished body with `shape_check.check`. Prompts should use `SectionSpec.summary` and `FieldSpec.satisfies`/`FieldSpec.bullet()` for constrained fields; for acceptance criteria, ask for checkable outcomes and explicitly say implementation steps, file paths, call sequences, and design plans belong later. Do not present `SEED_VOCABULARY` or any closed observable-verb list. Return a result that distinguishes complete/runnable output from incomplete draft output and carries remaining `Reason.code`/detail values from the same gate evaluation.

steps.description: Add a thin CLI command for interactive authoring and pre-submit validation.
steps.details: Add `forge author` with options for starting fresh, loading `--from-draft PATH`, loading an existing draft issue with `--from-issue N`, writing `--output PATH`, and submitting with `--create`. The command should collect missing required parts interactively, show the relevant constraint at the prompt for that part, run the authoring-flow validation before any `gh issue create` or `gh issue edit`, and refuse to submit when the result is not runnable. For incomplete results, write a draft instead: preserve existing prose through the typed document round trip, include the current title/labels metadata when writing a file, keep or add `todo:draft`, and add an obvious incomplete marker/status so the body does not read as ready.

steps.description: Wire the command into the existing CLI tree.
steps.details: Import the new `author` module, register its parser in `build_parser()`, add `author.cmd_author` to the command dispatch map, and re-export `cmd_author` from `cli/__init__.py` following the existing shape/groom/todo patterns.

steps.description: Keep the shape gate aligned with the no-closed-vocabulary contract.
steps.details: Verify the issue-2725 state is present: `check_no_observable_done_state` should only enforce structural absence of an acceptance-criteria section or bullets, not match acceptance bullets against `SEED_VOCABULARY`. If the dependency branch still has vocabulary-based refusal, retire that branch from admission while preserving structural missing-AC findings and existing semantic review paths.

steps.description: Document the new authoring surface where authors already look.
steps.details: Add a concise `forge author` section that points authors to the interactive path before filing, describes fresh authoring and completing `todo:draft`/local drafts, and states the constraints in property form: required parts come from the typed issue spec, acceptance criteria should be reviewer-checkable outcomes, and implementation-plan details belong outside the issue body. Do not duplicate the type table or verb vocabulary; link to the generated issue-shape reference if needed.

steps.description: Add focused regression tests for the core flow and CLI.
steps.details: Cover a complete enhancement/task body produced by the authoring flow passing `shape_check.check` without requiring a fixed observable verb, a required part declined producing an incomplete `todo:draft` result rather than runnable output, an existing draft body being parsed and preserved while missing sections are collected, and CLI behavior that writes/edits/creates only after validation. Add or adjust shape-check assertions so an AC bullet can be admitted structurally without matching `SEED_VOCABULARY`, while empty/missing AC still fails.

criteria_mapping.criterion: An authoring path exists that collects a body's required parts before submission and reports what is still missing, so an author is never refused for a rule they had no way to read.

Where a required part has a constrained form, the constraint is stated at the point that part is collected, expressed as the property the part must have rather than as an enumeration the author selects from. An acceptance criterion asks for an outcome a reviewer could check, and structural admission never depends on matching a fixed vocabulary — the authoring path does not make the author select from a word list, and no closed list is presented as the definition of observable. Whether a criterion is meaningful remains a semantic question, which review may still challenge.

A body produced through the authoring path passes the shape gate without a rewrite loop, and where it cannot, the path reports which part is still short rather than emitting a body that will be refused.

The authoring path parses and renders through the shared typed specification rather than carrying its own idea of the required parts, and validates the finished object through the same evaluation every other surface consumes before it submits anything.
The authoring path accepts an existing draft as a starting point, so a captured todo can be completed rather than restarted.
Where an author declines to supply a required part, the path writes a draft that is honestly marked incomplete rather than one that reads as ready.

risks.description: The story depends on issue-2725; if the typed specification or structural-only observable check is not actually present on the implementation base, the authoring flow would either duplicate contract data or still be blocked by the old verb vocabulary.
risks.mitigation: Treat issue-2725 as a hard prerequisite and make the dev agent verify `issue_spec.py`, `document.py`, and `check_no_observable_done_state` before implementing the new path.

risks.description: Interactive CLI behavior is harder to test cleanly than pure formatting logic.
risks.mitigation: Keep collection decisions in `intake/authoring_flow.py` with injected answers and reserve `cli/author.py` for argparse, prompts, file writes, and `gh` calls that can be monkeypatched like existing `test_cli_shape.py` and `test_cli_groom.py`.

risks.description: Supporting both local drafts and GitHub todo drafts could grow into a broad issue-management command.
risks.mitigation: Limit this slice to loading a draft, collecting missing typed parts, validating, writing an incomplete draft, or submitting/editing a validated body; leave prioritization, milestones, and broader todo triage to existing `forge todo`/`forge groom` flows.
